heroHeadline: Board of Peace Issues Ultimatum to Hamas: Disarm or Lose Ceasefire Guarantees — IDF Strikes Kill 9 in Three Days
heroSubtitle: The Trump-backed Board of Peace formally published a 'comply or else' ultimatum to Hamas on May 6, 2026, warning it would no longer hold Israel to ceasefire commitments if Hamas rejected the five-stage disarmament roadmap — as talks entered a full impasse on May 5 with Hamas, PIJ, and PFLP unanimously refusing. IDF strikes on May 6 killed Hamas anti-narcotics police colonel Naseem al-Kalazani near al-Mawasi and injured Azzam Al-Hayya, son of chief Hamas negotiator Khalil Al-Hayya — the fourth family member of the negotiating team harmed by Israeli fire. Four more Palestinians were killed in IDF strikes on May 7, bringing the cumulative death toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to 834+. On the Israeli political front, Justice Minister Yariv Levin threatened on May 7 to allow the Supreme Court to 'go extinct' if sitting justices blocked his judicial appointments — reigniting the 2023 judicial overhaul crisis ahead of expected October 2026 elections. UNRWA warned of a 'new humanitarian emergency within the ceasefire' with 45% of medicines out of stock and only one excavator in Gaza for body recovery. Flotilla activists Abu Keshek and Ávila remain detained without charge until at least May 10 despite UN demands for their immediate release.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, NPR, RTÉ, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
